items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: The original tuxedo band. Who was the leader of that band? Papa Celestine.

ctx.x: You see, when I was a boy, the brass bands of them days, they didn't play this orchestration numbers like these bands play on the street now. That's why we fight so hard to keep the brass bands like they should be. You see, that's like they kid me and tell me that I'll walk ten miles to get a march. In other words, kid me, but I don't walk. I wrote to every house there is to get a certain funeral march and I can't get it. I've asked Mr. Russell. I've asked Mr. Crawford. I've asked this boy Meads in Omaha,…
And when you were a boy you said they didn't play orchestrations? They didn't have? Not on the street.

items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: Well, let me see. They had us, they had John,

ctx.x: How many did Celestan's funeral have? Three or?
Well, let me see. They had us, they had John,

and I think. Two fifteen men bands. That was the way it was. That's the way it was. But it was just two. Yeah, two or two. Thirty men in all. That's all. And they just added on to the band. That's right. That's right. Do you remember Buddy Petit's funeral?
